newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras - EU farm reform sidelines Blair House.
newsitem.headline: Legras - EU farm reform sidelines Blair House.

text.p: A landmark 1992 trade pact between the European Union and the United States on oilseeds production would be sidelined by the EU's planned new farm reform, a senior EU farm official said on Monday.

European Commission agriculture director general Guy Legras said the Blair House agreement which limits EU oilseeds plantings would effectively disappear because there would no longer be a separate aid regime for European oilseeds producers.

"Blair House fixed an oilseeds area (for the EU) based on the fact that oilseeds had their own level of aid. When oilseeds no longer have their own aid, the conditions of Blair House disappear," he said.
Legras said he expected this to provoke some opposition in the United States but he believed that the world market for oilseeds was growing and this expansion would continue.
Under the farm reform known as Agenda 2000 the European Commission has proposed a single area aid payment of 66 Ecus a tonne for both oilseeds and cereals.
This compares with previous levels of 94 Ecus for oilseeds and 54.35 Ecus for cereals. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
